焦慮可以在，方向盤在自己手上｜2026.11: Anxiety can stay; the steering wheel stays in your own hands | 2026.11
「我就意識到，好像真的不需要焦慮耶，也不需要恐懼。其實我們就是也可以尊重自己會焦: "I realized that I really don't need to be anxious, and I don't need to be afraid. We can respect that we get anxious, respect that we get scared; that's just being human. But you need to know: don't let it lead you around. That is what we call seeing, and it is also what Frequency Civilization calls the steering layer."
看見，和把情緒壓下去，是兩件事。: Seeing, and pushing a feeling down, are two different things.
焦慮來了，我們不用假裝它不在，也不用責怪自己怎麼又焦慮了。這就是人會有的反應。: When anxiety shows up, we don't have to pretend it isn't there, and we don't have to scold ourselves for being anxious again. It's simply a reaction people have.
我們只需要多做一步：知道它在，聽聽它想說什麼，然後由現在的自己決定，要不要照著它: We only need to do one more thing: know that it's there, listen to what it's trying to say, and then let the present self decide whether or not to act on it.
在我們的世界觀裡，這一步叫治理層。: In our worldview, this step is called the steering layer.
意思很簡單：心裡所有的聲音都可以說話。擔心、害怕、直覺、期待，我們都願意聽。: The idea is simple: every voice inside is allowed to speak. Worry, fear, intuition, hope: we're willing to hear all of them.
但方向盤還是在現在的你手上，做了決定，後果也由現在的你承擔。: But the steering wheel stays in the hands of the present you, and once you decide, the present you carries the consequences too.
半夜睜著眼睛，腦子裡一直想著明天的會議。: Lying awake at midnight, your mind keeps running tomorrow's meeting.
以前可能有兩種做法：硬要自己別想（結果更睡不著），或是乾脆一路想下去（結果想到三: There used to be two options: force yourself not to think about it (and sleep even less), or just keep thinking (until three in the morning).
看見，是第三種：「我在怕明天講不好。」就這一句。: Seeing is a third option: "I'm afraid I'll speak badly tomorrow." Just that one sentence.
事情沒有變，但你從「被焦慮推著走的人」，慢慢變成「知道自己正在焦慮的人」。: Nothing has changed, but you slowly shift from "someone pushed around by anxiety" to "someone who knows they are anxious."
這兩個人，隔天早上做的決定，可能就會不一樣。: Those two people may well make different decisions the next morning.
研究參考｜接納與標記情緒: Research reference | Accepting and labeling emotions
60 位有焦慮或情緒困擾的人，看一段會引起情緒的影片。事前被告知「接納情緒」的那: Sixty people with anxiety or mood difficulties watched an emotionally provoking film. The group told beforehand to "accept" their emotions showed a drop in heart rate afterward and recovered from negative feelings faster; the group told to "suppress" them showed a rise in heart rate. During the film itself, both groups reported similar distress; the difference appeared in the recovery afterward. (Campbell-Sills, Barlow, Brown & Hofmann, Behaviour Research and Therapy, 2006)
給情緒一個名字，本身就有作用。腦部造影研究裡，當人用一個詞標出看到的負面情緒（例: Giving an emotion a name does something on its own. In a brain-imaging study, when people labeled a negative emotion they saw with a single word (for example, "angry"), activity in the amygdala, which is linked to emotional reactions, went down, while activity in a prefrontal region involved in regulation went up. (Lieberman et al., Psychological Science, 2007)
把 151 篇研究合起來看，「心理不彈性」（被想法和感受牽著走、為了逃避它們而放: Pooling 151 studies, people higher in "psychological inflexibility" (being led around by thoughts and feelings, and giving up what matters in order to avoid them) had poorer well-being, with a correlation of about −0.47. This is cross-sectional data: it can only say the two are related, not which causes which. (Ong, Barthel & Hofmann, Behavior Therapy, 2024)
這裡想說清楚一件事：這些研究談的是「接納與標記情緒」這個做法，並沒有在證明治理層: One thing we want to make clear: these studies are about the practice of "accepting and labeling emotions." They do not prove the idea of a steering layer.
治理層是我們理解這件事的框架；而這些研究，是我們選擇這個做法的理由之一。: The steering layer is the framework we use to understand this; these studies are one of the reasons we chose this practice.
Lieberman M.D. 等 (2007). Putting feeling: Lieberman M.D. et al. (2007). Putting feelings into words: Affect labeling disrupts amygdala activity in response to affective stimuli. Psychological Science, 18(5), 421–428.
「其實會發生事情就一定會發生啦，而且大節點就改不了嘛。可是你改變的是那個狀態跟小: "What is going to happen will happen anyway, and the big turning points can't be changed. What you change is the state you're in, and the small turning points. How do you change them? By remembering, anytime and anywhere, to return to who you originally are, your truest self. And being your truest self means: don't lie to yourself, and don't run away. Then face what needs facing, clear what needs clearing. It may hurt, but it hurts only once. If you avoid it, it hurts many times, and in the end you still have to face it."
這一段有兩層，我們分開慢慢講。: This passage has two layers, and we'll take them slowly, one at a time.
第一層是信念：有些處境，我們選不了。但我們怎麼回應，會影響這段經歷最後變成什麼。: The first layer is a belief: some situations we don't get to choose. But how we respond shapes what the experience finally becomes.
這是我們的看法，並非研究結論。: This is our view, not a research conclusion.
我們也不會拿這句話去解釋別人的痛。沒有人有資格對一個正在受苦的人說「這是你該遇到: We also don't use this sentence to explain other people's pain. No one has the right to tell someone who is suffering, "This is what you were meant to go through."
第二層是做法，而且是可以回頭檢查的。: The second layer is a practice, and one you can check later.
那些一直拖著、不敢面對的事，不會因為我們拖著，就慢慢變小。: The things we keep putting off and don't dare to face don't slowly shrink just because we keep putting them off.
它可能會換一種方式回來，而且常常是一次又一次地回來。: They may come back in a different form, and often again and again.
想想那通拖了三個禮拜，一直不敢打的電話。: Think of that phone call you've put off for three weeks, the one you don't dare to make.
這三個禮拜裡，每天想到一次，心口就緊一下。算一算，大概已經緊了二十幾次。: Over those three weeks, you think of it once a day, and each time your chest tightens. Add it up: it has tightened twenty-some times already.
真的打了，可能難受十分鐘。: When you finally make the call, it might feel bad for ten minutes.
「痛那麼一次」和「痛好幾次」，差別就在這裡。: That is the difference between "hurting that one time" and "hurting many times."
一連串研究把「拖延」理解成一種逃避：不想面對會帶來不舒服的事，就先把它推開。合起: A line of research understands "procrastination" as a form of avoidance: we push away things that would feel uncomfortable to face. Taken together, habitual procrastinators report more stress, and what mainly explains the link is the path of "coping with emotions by avoiding them." (Sirois & Kitner, European Journal of Personality, 2015)
2025 年一篇跨樣本的統合分析發現，長期拖延和自評健康較差有關，其中一部分可以: A 2025 multi-sample meta-analysis found that chronic procrastination is associated with poorer self-rated health, and that part of this can be explained by higher stress. (Sirois & Monaghan, British Journal of Health Psychology, 2025)
這兩篇研究談的是拖延與壓力，可以支持「該面對就面對」這個做法。: These two papers are about procrastination and stress, and they support the practice of "facing what needs facing."
至於「大節點改不了」，那是我們的信念。研究沒有、也不會去證明這件事。: As for "the big turning points can't be changed," that is our belief. Research has not proven it, and will not.
「既然大家都是人，就一定會犯錯，也一定會不完美，大家一定要有這個認知。所以相對來: "Since we are all human, we will all make mistakes and all be imperfect; everyone needs to understand this. So, by the same token, don't hand this work over to someone else to do for you. I actually think that treating someone as a hero, or holding overly high expectations of them, is rather irresponsible, because part of it is wanting to dump our own work, the work we can't do, onto someone else. We can hold it in a beautiful way: if someone else can do it, that's a bonus, and they are a role model. But don't make everything depend on them; that is attachment. The process of attachment is you continually handing your own power away, giving it to someone else."
欣賞一個人，和把自己交給一個人，中間其實有一條線。: Between admiring someone and handing yourself over to someone, there is a line.
線的這邊：他做得到，很好，我可以看著他學。: On this side of the line: they can do it, good, I can watch and learn.
線的那邊：他會幫我決定、他知道我該怎麼活、沒有他我不行。: On the other side: they'll decide for me, they know how I should live, I can't manage without them.
過了這條線，就成了依附。: Cross that line, and it becomes attachment.
依附最需要留意的地方，是每一次，你都把「自己判斷」這件事往外推了一點。: What needs the most care about attachment is that each time, you push the task of "judging for yourself" a little further outward.
推久了，那個原本會自己判斷的你，就越來越少有機會練習了。: Push it long enough, and the you who used to judge for yourself gets fewer and fewer chances to practice.
這條線，也不只存在於老師和學生之間。: This line doesn't only exist between teachers and students.
對伴侶、對老闆、對一個很會講話的朋友，甚至對 AI，其實都一樣。: With a partner, a boss, a very persuasive friend, even with AI, it is really the same.
每次遇到事情，第一個反應，就是傳訊息問那個人「我該怎麼辦」。: Whenever something happens, your first reaction is to message that person: "What should I do?"
他回了，你就照做；他沒回，你就整天不安。: If they reply, you do as they say; if they don't, you feel uneasy all day.
直到有一天，他說錯了，你也照做了。: Until one day they get it wrong, and you follow anyway.
這才發現，自己連「這聽起來對不對」，都沒有停下來想過。: Only then do you notice that you never even paused to ask, "Does this sound right?"
那一刻，也許很值得回頭問問自己：我把哪一塊功課，交出去太久了？: That moment may be worth a look back: which piece of my own work have I been handing out for too long?
研究參考｜焦慮時的判斷，與控制感: Research reference | Judgment under anxiety, and a sense of control
八個實驗發現，人在焦慮的時候，對自己比較沒信心，所以更會去找人問、也更會照著別人: Eight experiments found that when people are anxious, they have less confidence in themselves, so they seek advice more and follow it more. More importantly, anxious people fail to tell good advice from bad, and they keep listening even when the advisor has an obvious conflict of interest. (Gino, Brooks & Schweitzer, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 2012)
「無助」這件事被研究了五十年。原本的理論是「無助是學來的」；2016 年兩位原作: "Helplessness" has been studied for fifty years. The original theory was that "helplessness is learned." In 2016 the two original authors revisited the neuroscience evidence and revised their account: when faced with something we can't control, passivity is the default response; what is actually learned is the experience that "I can influence the outcome." This conclusion comes mainly from animal research, and whether it transfers directly to humans is still being debated. (Maier & Seligman, Psychological Review, 2016)
這兩篇研究談的是：人在焦慮時，比較容易把判斷交給別人。而「自己能影響結果」的感覺: These two papers say: when people are anxious, they more easily hand their judgment to others, and the sense that "I can influence the outcome" can be built up slowly.
它們可以支持「功課自己做」這個做法，但沒有在證明「力量」究竟是什麼。: They support the practice of "doing your own work," but they do not prove what "power" ultimately is.
這些是我們的觀察與信念，不是研究結論。: These are our observations and beliefs. They are not research conclusions.
焦慮和恐懼是人性的一部分，不用急著消滅。看見它，也練習不被它牽著走，就夠了。: Anxiety and fear are part of being human; there's no rush to get rid of them. Seeing them, and practicing not being led around by them, is enough.
心裡所有的聲音，都值得被好好聽見。但決定權還是在現在的自己手上，做了決定，也願意: Every voice inside deserves to be heard properly. But the decision still rests with the present self, and once a decision is made, we're willing to carry its consequences.
有些處境，我們選不了，但怎麼回應，還是可以自己選。我們改不了大節點，卻可以決定自: Some situations we can't choose, but we can still choose how to respond. We can't change the big turning points, but we can decide how we walk through them.
成長不必等到崩潰。「我選擇不再以痛來成長，我選擇用愛、智慧、穩定完成我的進化。」: Growth doesn't have to wait for a breakdown. "I choose to no longer grow through pain. I choose to complete my evolution with love, wisdom, and steadiness." (Molly, personal notes, 2025-04, translated from Chinese)
把判斷權留在自己手上。好的老師、課程和工具，會讓你越用越不需要它。「真正的頻率教: Keep the power of judgment in your own hands. Good teachers, courses and tools make you need them less the more you use them. "Real frequency education is what makes you clearer, freer, and less and less in need of me." (Molly, post, 2025-09, translated from Chinese)
「世界不需要英雄，需要的是更多清醒並且願意為自己負責的人。」（Molly・口述・: "The world doesn't need heroes. It needs more people who are awake and willing to take responsibility for themselves." (Molly, spoken, 2026-11-13, translated from Chinese)
讀到這裡，可以先停一下，把這三句話存起來。下次心口又緊起來的時候，拿出來，慢慢問: If you've read this far, pause for a moment and keep these three sentences. The next time your chest tightens, take them out and ask yourself, slowly:
我現在在怕什麼？: What am I afraid of right now?
這件事裡，哪一部分是我的功課？: Which part of this is my own work?
我正在把力量交給誰？: Who am I handing my power to?

The anxiety and fear discussed here refer to the everyday emotional reactions most people have; if they have been affecting your sleep, work or relationships for a while, please reach out to professional medical or mental-health resources.
